text:
Maya R: sharing results from a 10k bring-up smoke for rift11k (11B) comparing int6 vs int8 on our webchat slice. big picture: int6 saves a lot but we see non-negligible quality regressions concentrated on longform abstractive tasks. full thread below.

Jin Park: thanks — high level numbers first pls.

Maya R: short summary from eval-bot (paste):

eval-bot: summary: sample_n=10000, cost_change=-28% (int6 vs int8), qa_accuracy_change=-1.8pp, hallucination_change=+2.1pp, p95_latency_change=+12ms

Maya R: quick table we used (rounded):
```
variant        cost_per_1k_tokens  QA_acc  halluc_rate  p95_latency
rift11k-int8   $0.84               82.1%   3.2%         220ms
rift11k-int6   $0.61               80.3%   5.3%         232ms
```

Oliver H: ugh, +2.1pp hallucination — where are those coming from? long-context only?

Maya R: yep. slice breakdown: longform summaries (>2k tokens) account for ~65% of halluc increases. short Q&A and code tasks stay ~flat (~0.4-0.6pp drop).

Jin Park: any priming/temperature tuning tried? sometimes int configs mis-calibrate.

Maya R: tried stronger grounding prompts and a mild temp reduction (0.7->0.5). recovered ~0.6pp hallucination but hurt QA by ~0.4pp. reranking helps (1.5pp improvement in halluc but +6% cost).

Ava: from GTN/product: we care about unit econ and safe defaults. what's the recommended rollout?

Maya R: proposal: default to int6 for "short" endpoints (<2k tokens) and keep int8 for longform features. Canary 5% -> 25% over 2 weeks. Gate on hallucination_rate and QA_delta.

Jin Park: simulated routing with length-based rule: if prompt_tokens > 2000 -> int8 else int6. sim command we ran: 
```bash
python tools/sim_routing.py 
  --trace traces/webchat_10k.json 
  --policy "len>2000->int8;else->int6" 
  --out reports/rift11k_lenroute.json 
  --metrics cost,qa_acc,halluc_rate,p95
```
Result: effective cost_per_1k ~ $0.66 (vs $0.84 baseline) -> ~21-22% savings; net hallucination slightly above baseline but within product guardrails for routed mix.

Maya R: quick unit-econ note for GTN (assume avg tokens/req=1.5k):
- baseline all-int8: cost_per_1k=$0.84 -> cost_per_req ~= $1.26 -> per_1M_req ~= $1,260
- length-hybrid (80% short/int6,20% long/int8): effective cost_per_1k~$0.66 -> cost_per_req ~= $0.99 -> per_1M_req ~= $990
- delta ~= $270 saved per 1M requests (~21.4% savings)

Ava: tidy. callout: those numbers assume our current token distribution. if product increases context lengths or adds system prompts, savings drop. will flag in GTN note.

Oliver H: ops items: we need per-variant telemetry (hallucination, QA slices, p95 latency) and billing tags for variant. fallback policy: if hallucination_rate > 5% sustained over 5m -> automatic revert to all-int8.

Maya R: agree. I'll add the per-slice CSV and sim config to the draft doc.

Jin Park: I'll sketch a smoke harness that runs on canary traffic and emits the hallucination metric + slice breakdown. can wire to alerting.

Ava: please also include an exec blurb for GTN. short paragraph + the unit econ numbers. product wants language they can give to customers.

Maya R: proposed exec blurb: "Recommend a staged launch: enable int6 as the cost-default for short, cost-sensitive endpoints while routing long-context/abstractive features to int8. In simulation this hybrid approach delivered ~21% model-spend savings while keeping critical longform quality close to baseline. Start with a 5% canary widening to 25% over two weeks with tight signal gates (hallucination, QA-slice regression, p95 latency). If hallucination exceeds 5% for 5 minutes, fallback to all-int8."

Jin Park: small note: reranker as mitigation is effective but increases unit cost ~6%. If we combine rerank only on longform outputs we keep cost impact <2.5% overall.

Oliver H: next steps (owners):
- Maya: attach per-slice CSV, sim configs, and example prompt samples (EOD).
- Jin: smoke harness for canary metrics + quick runbook (48h).
- Ops: add billing tags and implement fallback alarm (prio-high).
- Ava: finalize GTN playbook and customer-facing language; confirm canary % (5->25).

Ava: will confirm with GTN and schedule the playbook review. thanks all. :rocket:

Maya R: linking draft after I upload files. will ping when done.

Jin Park: +1 happy to help integrate the harness.

Oliver H: LGTM. if we see halluc spikes during canary we rollback and run a short blameless investigation.

eval-bot: uploaded artifacts -> s3://redwood-eval/rift11k/1765439999/ (includes per-slice CSV, sim config, and top-100 failure examples)

Maya R: end.
